newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania jails eight ex-communists, acquits one.
newsitem.headline: Albania jails eight ex-communists, acquits one.

text.p: An Albanian court sentenced eight ex-communists on Wednesday to up to 22 years in jail for ordering thousands of dissidents into internal exile before the demise of Albania's communist regime in 1990.
Chief judge Andi Celiku acquitted a ninth man, Pali Miska, accused of crimes against humanity due to a lack of evidence that any citizen had been deported during his period in office.
"He is declared innocent because there were no criminal consequences for lack of proof," Celiku said.
It was the first time in five trials of former communist officials that any defendant had been acquitted, but Miska must still serve out a prison term for a previous sentence for abuse of power.
Miska was party head in the Fieri district in South-West Albania and a member of the political bureau, the communist party elite headed by the late dictator Enver Hoxha.
The other eight were either secret police chiefs or party heads in different cities, or senior officials in the interior ministry.

Around 100,000 Albanians are believed to have been forced into exile in remote villages during 45 years of communist rule because of their alleged opposition to the Stalinist government or for trying to escape from the isolated Balkan country.

Three senior ex-communists were sentenced to death in May but an appeals court revoked the sentences and imposed jail terms instead. Thirteen other ex-communists have been sentenced to up to 25 years in jail for crimes against humanity.
No date has yet been set for the trial of former president Ramiz Alia and two former interior ministers charged with ordering the shooting of Albanians who tried to flee the country.
